description: FTLR-0 / SCIP-PILOT formal anchor registry (issue #299). This file is the SOLE cross-domain authority binding C++ semantic authorities to formal claims. C++-internal relationships are never recorded here; they are recovered mechanically from the SCIP index (scip-clang over the Xmake compile_commands.json). Suite ids must match spec/tla/manifest.json. Claim ids follow the S1A property matrix (docs/investigations/s1a-formal-coverage.md); F02/F05/F07/F09/F10 are intentionally not seeded in this pilot (bounded corpus). This registry is experiment-scoped: it is a precursor schema for the #298 FDG-0 correspondence registry, not a replacement for any existing authority.

claims.title: request identity / generation / stale reuse

cpp_anchors.note: identity gate: stale-generation / free / out-of-range handles rejected before any slot transition
generation advance before freed slot re-enters the free list

claims.notes: Contract: stable K=(context,slot,generation); generation++ BEFORE freed slot re-enters free list; stale g can never mutate/terminalize/observe the new occupant. Residual: multi-slot interleavings = executable-evidence scope (manifest coverage_gaps).

claims.title: terminal winner / exactly-once

cpp_anchors.note: first backend_ready terminal wins under the leaf mutex; losers never overwrite
blocking backend producer of real terminals

io_uring backend producer of real terminals. The default xmake config compiles this TU in UNSUPPORTED-STUB mode (the terminal machinery is compiled out), so this anchor resolves only in an index built with `xmake f --with-liburing=y`. A default-config check reports it as a config-gated unresolved anchor: a visible declared gap, not a silent miss.

claims.notes: Contract: exactly one terminal per accepted generation; Scheme-B single-domain arbitration. Model coverage spans request-arena (NEG-RA-1), e10-waitnode (primitive domain), e13 select winner linearization.

claims.title: Completion publication

cpp_anchors.note: the only path that may drive a caller-owned Completion to ready (through the installed CompletionBinding thunk)
single release-store linearization point of Completion-ready (template member; grep-audited single invoker)

claims.notes: Contract: only the designated reap path makes a caller-owned Completion ready; ready release-store is the single LP; observer of ready sees result + closed registration + retired accounting + ended borrow. Memory-order face: GenMC K1/K2 (#197, spec/weakmem). Protocol face: request-arena NEG-RA-3 + f1-wait-record E7-T2.

claims.title: cancel vs ordinary completion

cpp_anchors.note: single disposition authority: pending/enqueued cancel may win the terminal (Scheme B); running cancel records intent only
stale generation => not_found; SHARED anchor with F01 (deliberate T5 shared-authority specimen)
task-layer request-epoch advance (single CAS with rearm); defined out-of-line in cancel.cpp
free friend function (not a member): single-shot delivery per epoch per consumer between the two explicit re-arm authorities; reads ONE atomic snapshot

claims.notes: Contract: layered cancellation; kernel-owned cancel CQE is control-informational; terminal => already_terminal. Weak-memory face of the token EVALUATED NOT REQUIRED (S1A argument-based; reopen triggers recorded in F06/B).

claims.title: wait / wake / lost-wakeup closure

cpp_anchors.note: unified wake source: every progress-enabling publication routes here; advances wake_epoch_ and notifies the wake domain
park commit: epoch predicate, split-wait bridge, MW-S2/S3 classification
R-F1 per-thread startup publication (active.store(true)) and the Settled-gated run_impl join boundary
the monotonically-advanced wake epoch field itself (state authority; catches direct writers that bypass the wake functions)

claims.notes: Contract: every progress-enabling change declares persistent predicate/producer/consumer/signal/commit-to-sleep closure. Claim boundary (R-F1 #223): post-settlement TRANSITION-SCHEMA correspondence, NOT reachable-state or behavioral refinement; startup population modeled with FairStartWorker as a host/environment liveness assumption. wake_epoch_ is anchored as a STATE authority so a new writer that bypasses signal_wake_locked is still structurally reachable (T9 design finding).
